classification.difficultyReason: Apply the polynomial division identity at both roots of a quadratic divisor, then solve simultaneously for two coefficients.

content.prompt: The remainder when $x^5-3x^2+ax+b$ is divided by $(x-1)(x-2)$ is $11x-10$. Find $a$ and $b$.

answer.short:
$a=-11$, $b=14$.

Substitute $x=1$ and $x=2$ into the division identity and solve simultaneously.
answer.worked:
Let $P(x)=x^5-3x^2+ax+b$. The division identity gives
$$P(x)=(x-1)(x-2)Q(x)+11x-10.$$
At $x=1$ and $x=2$, the quotient term vanishes. Thus
$$\begin{align*}P(1)&=11(1)-10\\P(1)&=1,\\1-3+a+b&=1\\a+b&=3.\qquad (1)\end{align*}$$
Similarly,
$$\begin{align*}P(2)&=11(2)-10\\P(2)&=12,\\32-12+2a+b&=12\\2a+b&=-8.\qquad (2)\end{align*}$$
Subtracting (1) from (2), then substituting into (1), gives
$$\begin{align*}a&=-8-3\\a&=-11,\\b&=3-(-11)\\b&=14.\end{align*}$$
